svg.title: How service secrets are stored and delivered
svg.text: How service secrets are stored and delivered
Secret values live in your own cloud account: Parameter Store on AWS, Secret Manager on Google Cloud. Example environment prefix: env-loc123, service: backend323.
• Encrypted at rest with KMS; decrypted only when read
• Standard tier up to 4 KB, Advanced tier up to 8 KB
• Tagged with the environment's resource tags
one per service, plus one for
• Service level wins on a key clash
one secret per key · automatic replication
• Encrypted at rest by Google; every update adds a version
• LocalOps always reads the latest version
one per service, plus one for
• Service level wins on a key clash
Save: each value is written straight to your cloud account. LocalOps keeps only the key name and a pointer (parameter ARN or secret resource name), never the value.
Sync: values are read back, decrypted and written into a Kubernetes Secret in your cluster. Your pods never call Parameter Store or Secret Manager.
Deploy: each key is mounted into your containers as an environment variable. Redeploy to pick up changed secrets.
